title: [Mobile and Compatibility] Light3D relative position, cull_mask and frustum cull being overridden by SubViewport cameras
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in 4.7, 4.7.2, **4.6.2, 4.3, 4.0.2, 4.0.1, 4.0.0,** with Mobile and Combatibility. - Not reproducible in 3.x (GLSL2) or any 4.x version with Forward+. ### System information Godot v4.7.2.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GT 710 (NVIDIA; 30.0.14.7514) - Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E5-2640 v3 @ 2.60GHz (16 threads) - 15.84 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description Edits: The bug became clearer to me. When the game has a Main camera, a SubViewport with UPDATE_MODE_ALWAYS set and with another camera, and a light culled (any type of cull) from the main camera, any mesh within the AABB of this light will render **as if it was being seen from the SubViewport's Camera.** You can also see the effect right on the editor, in the camera preview. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6136f33a-4960-49ba-ac72-585874ab8b28 ### Steps to reproduce EDIT: made it simpler to reproduce Make this configuration: - Set the renderer to compatibility or mobile - The main camera must ignore the cull layer where the light is set - The subviewport camera must be able to see the light - The mesh should be big enough - SubViewport render target update mode must be set to ALWAYS Two things will happen: 1) The light will render anyway. 2) The relative position of the light for the main camera will mimic the relative position of the light for the subviewport camera.** ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [sub-viewport-update-light-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32577527/sub-viewport-update-light-bug.zip) Explaining the flicker in this MRP version: since the camera is a bit too close to the light it will disable the frustum cull, preventing the bug for a few frames, 2 times during rotation. Just increase the distance from the main camera to the light and the flicker shouldn't occur. Make sure the floor is big enough to accommodate the relative distance from the subviewport camera to the light. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16d8041c-60dd-477b-b7e1-dc2c240759a9 The bug gets weirder when we add another light in front of the main camera but outside the SubViewport camera's frustum. Represented by the purple light in the MRP demo. Notice the purple light increasing brightness, instead of the yellow light shining where it shouldn't.
